transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-14 09:00 PDT | Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Tandem Head of ML), Marcus Hale (Tandem Platform Eng), Sofia Alvarez (Tandem PM)

Summary: Short POC scoping to align on success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, and integration approach (OpenAI-compatible endpoints, SDKs, function/tool calling, structured JSON output). Discussed timelines and next steps for a 4-week pilot.

Topics: success criteria; throughput & latency targets; sample prompts and benchmark design; OpenAI-compatible SDK usage; function-calling/tool integration; VPC/KMS and privacy; SOW and timeline.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh appreciate you making time. Quick roll call — I'll let people say hi.
[00:06] Priya: Hi this is Priya, Head of ML at Tandem.
[00:09] Marcus: Marcus here, platform eng, I own infra.
[00:11] Sofia: Sofia, product.
[00:12] Liam: Liam, SE from Redwood.
[00:14] Maya: Great. Goal for today is to scope the POC: what success looks like, the workloads we should benchmark, and how you want to integrate — SDKs or direct OpenA I compatible calls, and function/tool calling.
[00:28] Priya: Yeah we want something bite-sized. Primary success is that we can meet our internal latency SLOs and keep token cost acceptable. Rough target is p95 latency below 300ms for short chat flows and throughput about 50 QPS on peak.
[00:41] Marcus: Also security is key — we need VPC connectivity, customer-managed KMS, audit logs, and retention controls.
[00:48] Maya: Totally. For the POC we usually run a 3–4 week pilot: week 1 integration + baseline, week 2 benchmarking, week 3 tuning and validation, week 4 decisioning. We can compress but that's the standard.
[01:02] Sofia: Sounds fine. The immediate ask is that our devs can use existing OpenAI SDK calls where possible to minimize lift.
[01:09] Liam: That's supported — Redwood exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. You can point openai.ChatCompletion.create or the newer /v1/chat/completions to our URL and pass your API key; we also provide our official SDKs with examples for Python/TS.
[01:23] Priya: Quick question: how does function calling work? We rely on structured outputs to feed downstream services.
[01:27] Liam: We mirror OpenAI-style function calling: you declare a JSON schema, model returns structured JSON or a function call object. We also support tool-calling patterns — you can register tools that the model can invoke, and Redwood will surface the function call metadata in the response. There are slight differences in field names sometimes in the logs, the transcript recorder occasionally shows 'func-call' spelled oddly, but semantics are the same.
[01:46] Priya: Ok good. For benchmarks, we'll send a prompt set of ~200 examples of the primary flows (short chat, data extraction, reranking). Average prompt size is ~600 input tokens, expected output ~120 tokens. Target throughput peak 50 QPS with steady average ~15 QPS.
[02:02] Maya: Helpful — for sizing we typically ask for tokens/day too; with those numbers that comes to roughly 5–8M tokens per day depending on concurrency. We'll size a dedicated sandbox with a couple of GPU instances to hit 50 QPS for the POC.
[02:16] Marcus: On quantization and models: can we test multiple variants? We want to compare a float16 variant vs 4-bit quantized for cost/latency tradeoffs.
[02:23] Liam: Yep, we can run both. We'll recommend a shortlist of compatible open models and Redwood-verified performance profiles. For POC benchmarks we'll run: baseline unquantized, q4_0 quant, and a medium-latency low-cost variant. We'll track p50/p95, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens.
[02:39] Sofia: How about streaming and partial responses for UI? We need chunked streaming to show tokens as they arrive.
[02:44] Liam: Supported. We mirror streaming semantics like OpenA I: server-sent events or SDK streaming callbacks. Some customers use the SDK's stream handler, others use SSE. We'll include streaming tests in the benchmark.
[02:55] Priya: Security: does Redwood support customer KMS and private deployments? We have PCI-ish data in some transcripts so we need control.
[03:03] Maya: Yes — for POCs we can either spin a private VPC sandbox with peering or use a dedicated tenant with customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest. Audit logs and SOC 2 artifacts are available; we'll attach the security pack.
[03:13] Marcus: Ok we'll need the compliance pack and the KMS procedure. I'll add that to action items.
[03:18] Liam: On integration specifics: for minimal changes you can use the existing OpenAI SDK and only change the base_url and the key. Example we sent in the deck: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -X POST https://redwood.example/v1/chat/completions -d '{...}'. For function calling use the functions attribute like you do today.
[03:36] Priya: Any gotchas with rate limits or batching?
[03:39] Liam: We have per-tenant rate limits for hosted and additional burst options for Dedicated. For the POC we'll configure higher limits; Redwood supports automatic batching and prefix caching — that can dramatically reduce token cost for repeated prefixes. We'll test with and without caching.
[03:54] Maya: Success criteria recap? Priya you mentioned p95 < 300ms and cost within estimated budget. Anything else?
[04:00] Priya: Accuracy thresholds — extraction F1 above 0.88 on the sample set, and reranking NDCG within 5% of our current heuristic baseline.
[04:08] Sofia: Product acceptance: integration with our toolchain — we want function outputs in strict JSON to feed our orchestrator.
[04:15] Liam: We'll demonstrate structured output with enforced JSON schema and show function-call metadata. We'll also show rollback to a fallback model if a variant fails QA.
[04:24] Marcus: Network and infra: we'll need VPC peering, IP allowlist, and a contact for KMS provisioning. We might want to run a small on-prem instance if latency from our region is bad, but let's try VPC first.
[04:37] Maya: Timeline — we'll draft the SOW and target starting integration next Monday (2027-04-19). Benchmarks done by week two, tune week three, decision week four (by 2027-05-14). Does that align?
[04:49] Priya: Yes that's fine.
[04:50] Sofia: Works for product.
[04:51] Marcus: I'll coordinate infra availability during week one.
[04:55] Liam: Technical deep-dive — I propose we run two benchmarks: 1) latency p95 for chat at target QPS; 2) cost per 1k tokens across models/quant. We'll provide scripts plus an SDK snippet showing the OpenAI-compatible payload and function calling examples.
[05:11] Priya: For the benchmark script, please include the option to replay our traffic shape — bursts and steady state.
[05:16] Liam: Will do. Also note there may be slight naming mismatches in the logs (like K-V cache spelled K-V cache or KVcache) in our debug dumps; ignore those, it's just transcription/label differences.
[05:27] Maya: Ok let's recap next steps — Maya will send the SOW and pricing, Liam will send SDK snippets and benchmark scripts, Tandem will share prompt set and targets, Marcus shares infra/KMS info. We'll tentatively meet for the technical deep dive Tuesday 2027-04-20 10am PT.
[05:43] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks team.
[05:46] Sofia: Thanks, bye.
[05:47] Marcus: Bye.

End of call.
